The start of doctoral study is agreed upon with the supervisor and takes into consideration when funding becomes available, earliest in April for the summer semester and latest in October for the winter semester.
Applications must be submitted through our online application tool â submissions via mail or email cannot be accepted.
Applications that have not been formally submitted will not be reviewed.
Incomplete applications will not be considered and will be automatically deleted after 3 months in accordance with data protection regulations.
Only complete, submitted applications with 2 letters of reference will be considered !
There are no application or tuition fees.
All courses are held in English.
Steps
1. Register Online Create your account and confirm your registration via the link sent to your email.
Link to the application/registration portal
2. Log In & Complete Your Application Log in with your personal username and password to the LSM online application system and fill out the application form.
3. Upload Your Documents Upload all required documents directly in the application system.
4. Invite Your Referees Contact your referees and confirm they are willing to write a letter of recommendation on your behalf. Then enter their details in the references tab and click "Save" â this will automatically send them an invitation to submit their letter electronically. Please note: It is your responsibility to ensure your referees submit their letters on time.
5. Your application can be edited at any time before submission.
6. Submit Your Application Click the "Save and Submit" button in the upper menu to finalise your application.
Please note:
All fields marked with a yellow triangle are mandatory
Optional fields are encouraged â the more information you provide, the better we can assess your application
Once submitted, your application can no longer be edited (except name, password and email)
The LSM coordination office will verify completeness after submission
What Happens Next?
Receipt of your complete application will be confirmed in the "My Progress" section of your application form.
Each submitted letter of recommendation will be confirmed in the "My Progress" section and via email.
Your referee will also receive an email confirmation once their letter has been successfully received.
Selection Process
Applications are independently reviewed by several faculty members of the Graduate School LSM. Candidates are evaluated on the basis of:
Academic qualification, Research experience, Scientific background, Motivation, Letters of recommendation
Shortlisted candidates will be invited to our online interview days in January 2027.
Successful applicants will be offered a doctoral position, which is generally funded through the supervisor's third-party research funds or scholarships.

Applicants must hold one of the following degrees in biology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, biophysics, biotechnology, medicine, or a related discipline:
Master's degree (MSc) or German university Diploma
Bachelor's degree (BSc) with Honours (4-year degree with written thesis) â considered in exceptional cases only, awarded with a first class degree or, in rare cases, an upper second class degree (UK standard)
For BSc applicants, the degree must include a research project with written thesis, written or oral final examinations, and at least six months of advanced coursework.
The 4-year Bachelor's degree from the LMU faculty of Biology is accepted, but not the 3-year one.
The degree does not need to be completed at the time of application, but must be awarded before starting the doctoral studies.
The most recent final examination must have taken place no more than four years prior to the date of application.
Final eligibility decisions are made after submission of a complete application and require approval by university officials.
Language Requirements
All courses, lectures, and seminars are held in English. Selected candidates must be fluent in written and spoken English.
A TOEFL or IELTS certificate is strongly recommended, but not compulsory. It will strengthen your application but is not a criterion for exclusion.
A language certificate is not required if you:
Are a native English speaker
Completed your entire education in English
Studied for at least six months at an English-speaking institution
Can demonstrate proficiency through other means (e.g. German Abitur results)
Applicants from non-EU countries are strongly advised to submit a GRE test. For details, visit www.ets.org/gre.
Applicants from India may also submit GATE results.
Mandatory:
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Transcript of records and degree certificate â Bachelor's degree (min. 240 ECTS) or equivalent
Transcript of records and degree certificate â Master's degree or equivalent (if applicable; temporary transcripts accepted if degree is ongoing)
Two letters of recommendation (see other tab)
High school degree transcripts or equivalent
Letters of Motivation (max. 1 A4 page) â specifically addressing why you chose your selected projects. Generic statements will not be considered.
Recommended:
English language certificate (if applicable)
Evidence of scholarships, prizes or awards (if applicable)
GRE test (strongly recommended for non-EU applicants)
Two letters of recommendation are mandatory. At least one must be provided by your Bachelor's or Master's supervisor (based on your most recently awarded degree).
Before You Apply
Contact your referees before submitting your application to confirm they are willing to write a recommendation on your behalf. Once you enter their details in the online application form and submit, an automatic invitation is sent to each referee â this cannot be undone. It is not possible to change your choice of referee after the invitation has been sent.
How It Works
Letters of recommendation are submitted electronically by your referees directly through the online application system. Once your application is submitted, both you and your referee(s) will receive a confirmation email. The receipt of each letter is also reflected in the status box of your application form.
Important Deadlines & Responsibilities
Your application cannot be processed until both letters have been received.
Applications missing one or both letters after this deadline will be considered incomplete and will not be processed further.
It is your responsibility to ensure your referees submit their letters on time.
All letters of recommendation are treated with strict confidentiality.

LSM Application Decision Tree â Doctoral Program Munich
Step-by-step guide to applying for the Graduate School Life Science Munich
When completing the application form, you must select one of the following:
Internal candidate â You are already conducting your doctoral studies within an LSM group and are applying to join the Graduate School. Applications are accepted up to one year into the project. Proof of your first TAC meeting must be included.
or
External candidate â You are applying both to the Graduate School and for a doctoral position as listed on our doctoral projects page.
Enlarge
Â© Carolin Bleese
There are several ways to join the LSM doctoral programme.
All applications must be submitted through the LSM Online Application Portal, regardless of the funding route.
Doctoral Positions Some of our principal investigators (PIs) are in the process of securing third-party funding and are committed to supporting promising candidates in identifying and applying for appropriate funding for specific doctoral projects. These positions are advertised on our Open Positions page.
Independent Research Proposals If you have a strong research idea and are interested in working with a specific LSM group, we encourage you to reach out to the relevant group leader directly. If your proposal is a good fit, the group leader will support you in applying for a scholarship, fellowship, or third-party funding. All applications must then be formally submitted through the LSM online application portal.
Faculty Research Areas Open to Proposals
Other Funding options for national and international applicants
Chinese Applicants â CSC Scholarship Chinese doctoral candidates may be eligible for the LMU-CSC Scholarship (China Scholarship Council). The process works as follows:
Apply through the LSM Online Application Portal with your research idea or for specific doctoral project
Top candidates will be nominated by the LSM to the LMU-CSC programme
Nominated candidates will then be asked to submit a separate application through the LMU-CSC portal
For more information, please visit the LMU CSC Scholarship page or contact us.
